title: Audit and slimline token set for dense controls
creator: Ava Moreno
description: Consolidate and slim down the design token surface for high-density UI contexts (tables, compact forms, toolbars, and inline controls). Goals: reduce token count and cognitive surface for engineers, preserve WCAG AA contrast, improve runtime theming performance, and provide a 'dense' token mode for embedded widgets. Deliverables: token mapping table, migration guide, updated compact component specs (button, input, table row, chip), and QA checklist for color/contrast and motion implications.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Kickoff: Scoped to color palette pruning, typography micro-scale, radius compression, and shadow/elevation simplification for dense contexts. Cross-functional: Design, Platform, DevEx. Ava created initial audit spreadsheet in Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/design/token-audit-dense-v1

2025-02-18 - Audit complete: Identified ~68 tokens used only by legacy components and 12 near-duplicate semantic ramps. Proposal: merge to 22 semantic anchors for dense mode; keep full palette for normal density. See audit tab in spreadsheet.

2025-02-21 - Trade-off discussion with Platform: Reducing tokens will simplify runtime theme payloads (~25% smaller), but merging semantic ramps requires explicit contrast checks for states (hover/active/disabled). Platform asked for a machine-readable token map (JSON) and migration shim (runtime aliasing) to avoid breaking client integrations.

2025-02-26 - Design review: PM and accessibility lead reviewed compact radius proposal (4px -> 3px primary compact radius, 2px for micro controls) — approved pending accessibility contrast tests for focus rings and outline widths.

2025-03-01 - Engineering feasibility: ENG feedback: shadow flattening (reduce layers) yields measurable GPU paint improvement in lists; recommended removing soft blurred shadows in favor of 1 layered elevation token and a subtle overlay for active states. Eng requested implementation notes and a migration PR before rollout.

2025-03-03 - Prototype: Built compact tokens in Storybook with toggles (normal / compact). Early perf check (DevTools) shows 18% lower paint costs for dense lists. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui-stories/pull/412
2025-03-04 - Next steps: Prepare migration guide, add automated contrast tests to visual regression suite, and open design sign-off thread. Liam to own PRs and follow-up QA with QE.
notes: Migration plan: introduce `density` flag in token JSON (values: normal, compact). Runtime will resolve aliases; Platform will provide a compatibility shim for 3 releases.
Accessibility: run Axe color contrast checks plus manual verification for focus/keyboard states. Compact focus ring may need +1px width to remain visible on 3px radius controls.
Engineering: provide example tokens as flat alias map to avoid nested theme lookups in low-end clients.
QA checklist: verify table row heights, button hit areas, tooltip overlap, and elevation layering in Safari/Chrome/Firefox on macOS and Windows.
Rollback strategy: ship token aliases first (no component changes), then opt-in compact classes, then default the compact mode behind a runtime flag.
Estimated rollout timeline: aliasing and tests (2 weeks), component spec updates and PRs (1 week), QA and sign-off (1 week).
